weaknesses: The methodological advance is limited and insufficiently positioned. Much of the latent-space machinery comes from IG-AE, while the micro–macro decomposition is a shared linear dictionary concatenated with scene-specific features. The broader efficiency comparison is not performed at matched rendering quality. Table 4 reports only about 5% less training time than Instant-NGP, while PSNR falls from 37.71 to 31.20 dB. Tables 5–6 do not clearly establish whether first-subset results use the final shared parameters. Consequently, retaining all scenes after stage two, or after adding further scenes, is not adequately demonstrated.

Evaluation is restricted to 128×128 synthetic cars and front-facing faces, with quality measured on only 50 sampled scenes per dataset and no uncertainty estimates. Figure 5 follows assumed constant per-scene costs rather than demonstrating scaling across independently trained dataset sizes. Sensitivity to first-stage subset size, dictionary size, and feature allocation is also largely unexplored.
